common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Pelvic organ prolapse (uterine procidentia, Stage IV).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Cystocele/rectocele alone without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Complete uterine procidentia.

must_ask.say: How long have you felt this bulge, and does it get worse with standing or lifting?
Do you have trouble starting your urine stream, or leaking urine?
Do you have difficulty with bowel movements or need to push on your vagina to pass stool?
How many vaginal deliveries have you had, and were any of the babies large?
We can discuss a supportive pessary device or surgical repair depending on your preference.
